fact_text: For a China work assignment the employer, not the employee, must first obtain a Notification Letter of Foreigner's Work Permit through the online work-permit system; the employee then uses that letter to apply for the Z visa at a Chinese embassy/consulate.
evidence_quote: your employer can apply for a Notification Letter of Foreigner's Work Permit before you enter China

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you apply for a Chinese work visa yourself and sort out the job on arrival. Actually: your employer must first secure the Notification Letter of Foreigner's Work Permit via the government work-permit system before you can even apply for the Z visa. Action: have the employer file for the Notification Letter well before booking travel.

entity_title: Z visa to work-type residence permit (30 days)
fact_text: The Z visa is only an entry visa. A Z-visa holder (except very short-term work of no more than 30 days) must apply for a work-type Residence Permit for Foreigner at the local Public Security exit/entry authority within 30 days of entry; the residence permit, not the visa, authorises the stay.
evidence_quote: shall apply for Residence Permit for Foreigner in the People's Republic of China from the Exit/Entry Administrations of local Public Security within 30 days from the date of entry

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the Z visa lets you live and work in China for its whole validity. Actually: the Z visa is a single-entry entry visa; within 30 days of arrival you must convert it into a work-type residence permit at the PSB. Action: book the PSB residence-permit appointment in your first week in China.

fact_text: Any foreigner not staying in a hotel (e.g. a leased apartment or a friend's home) must register their accommodation, either personally or via the host, at the local police station within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels perform this registration automatically for their guests.
evidence_quote: Foreigners or the host shall go to the local police station for residence registration within 24 hours of arrival at their accommodation when they are not staying in a hotel.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the landlord or hotel handles registration, or you have several days to settle in. Actually: if you are not in a hotel, you or your host must register at the neighbourhood police station within 24 hours of arrival. Action: register within 24h of moving in, and re-register after every trip away.

entity_title: Work-permit talent tiers A / B / C
fact_text: Foreign workers are graded into Category A (high-end talent), B (professional) and C. Category A applicants scoring 85+ on the points table face no limits on age, education or work experience and get a fast-track 'green channel'; Category B typically needs a bachelor's degree plus two years' experience and a score of 60+.
evidence_quote: conform to the score-based system (scored 85 or above according to the Points-based Assignment Table), with no limits of age, academic qualification or work experience

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: there is one uniform 'China work visa'. Actually: foreigners are scored and classed A/B/C; Category A (85+ points) high-end talents get a green channel with no age/education/experience limit, while Category B professionals need a degree, 2 years' experience and 60+ points. Action: confirm which tier you qualify for before the employer files.

entity_title: IIT six-year rule on worldwide income
fact_text: A non-domiciled foreigner who is a Chinese tax resident is taxed on worldwide income only after residing in China 183+ days in each of six consecutive years without a single absence over 30 days; before that, foreign-source income paid abroad is exempt, and one trip abroad over 30 days in a year resets the six-year count.
evidence_quote: not left the country for more than 30 days in any of the previous six years, shall pay individual income tax originating both within and outside China

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: once you spend 183+ days in China you are immediately taxed on worldwide income. Actually: a non-domiciled resident's offshore-paid foreign income stays exempt until the 183-day threshold is met for six consecutive years, and a single trip abroad exceeding 30 days in any year resets the clock. Action: track your days and consider a >30-day trip before year six with a tax adviser.

entity_title: Work-type residence permit validity (90 days-5 years)
fact_text: A foreigner work-type residence permit can run from 90 days to a maximum of 5 years; the length granted depends on the holder's talent tier and the employer's track record, so a first permit is often only 1 year rather than the full assignment length.
evidence_quote: The shortest validity period for a foreigner work-type residence permit is 90 days and the longest period is 5 years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the residence permit is issued for the whole assignment or a standard multi-year term. Actually: a work-type residence permit ranges from 90 days to 5 years and is frequently issued for just 1 year at first, tied to tier and employer record. Action: plan for renewals and diarise the extension window (apply 30 days before expiry).

entity_title: Residence permit fees scale with validity
fact_text: The residence-permit fee is not flat: it is CNY 400 for a permit up to 1 year, CNY 800 for 1-3 years and CNY 1,000 for 3-5 years, and the same charge applies to every accompanying dependent added to the permit.
evidence_quote:
(1) For a residence permit valid for no more than 1 year: CNY 400 
 (2) For a residence permit valid for 1-3 years: CNY 800 
 (3) For a residence permit valid for 3-5 years: CNY 1,000

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the residence-permit fee is a single flat charge. Actually: the fee scales with validity (CNY 400 for <=1yr, 800 for 1-3yr, 1,000 for 3-5yr) and is charged again per accompanying family member. Action: budget the per-person fee for the whole family, not just the employee.

entity_title: Work permit is employer- and role-tied
fact_text: The work permit is bound to the specific employer and job in the registered employment contract. If the actual role becomes inconsistent with the approved one - anything other than a pay raise or a promotion - a fresh work-permit application is required.
evidence_quote: in cases of inconsistency, other than a pay raise or promotion of position, a new work permit application is required

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the work permit is a personal credential you keep when you change jobs or roles. Actually: it is tied to one employer and role; any change other than a pay raise or promotion requires a new work-permit application. Action: never switch employer or materially change role in China without re-filing the work permit first.

entity_title: Health certificate for permits over 1 year
fact_text: Applying for a residence permit valid for more than 1 year requires a health certificate from a Chinese health-and-quarantine authority (or a county-level+ medical institution) confirming the applicant is free of serious mental disorder, tuberculosis and other infectious diseases that could endanger public health.
evidence_quote: certifying that the applicant does not have serious mental disorder, tuberculosis or other infectious diseases which may potentially cause substantial hazard to public health

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: no medical check is needed for a corporate work move. Actually: any residence permit over 1 year requires a health/quarantine certificate ruling out serious mental disorder, TB and other infectious diseases, usually via a China inspection-and-quarantine exam after arrival. Action: budget time for the medical soon after you land.

fact_text: For a Category B work permit the applicant must submit an official no-criminal-record certificate issued within the last six months and authenticated by a Chinese embassy/consulate; a personal declaration or affidavit of good conduct is not accepted (Category A high-end talents may instead use a pledge system).
evidence_quote: A certificate of no criminal record issued within six months is valid. Personal declarations of no criminal record, for declaration only, are not accepted.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you can self-certify a clean criminal record. Actually: Category B applicants need an official police certificate issued within six months and consular-authenticated; a self-declaration is rejected. Action: start the police certificate plus authentication/legalisation early - it is one of the slowest steps.

entity_title: Mandatory social insurance for foreign employees
fact_text: Foreigners lawfully employed in China must participate in the local social insurance scheme (pension, medical, work-injury, unemployment and maternity); the employer must register the foreign employee within 30 days of processing their work permit, with both employer and employee contributing.
evidence_quote: foreigners employed in Beijing shall participate in the social insurance

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: foreign assignees are exempt from Chinese social insurance. Actually: foreigners lawfully employed in China must participate in social insurance and the employer must register them within 30 days of the work permit, unless a bilateral totalisation/exemption agreement applies. Action: check whether your home country has a social-security agreement with China before assuming exemption.
